classes.name: 立法會選舉
classes.locator: https://www.basiclaw.gov.hk/en/basiclaw/annex2.html (90 members: 40 returned by the Election Committee, 30 by functional constituencies, 20 by geographical constituencies through direct elections)
classes.note: One class for the whole council, because the geographical (directly elected), functional (sectoral electorates of individuals and corporate bodies), and Election Committee constituencies elect members of the same body on the same day and a selector cannot tell their contests apart. Seats: 60 in 1998-2008 (20, 24, 30 and 30 geographical; 10 and 6 Election Committee seats in 1998 and 2000), 70 in 2012-2016 (35 geographical, 35 functional including 5 District Council (second) seats elected territory-wide), and 90 from 2021 (20 geographical in 10 two-seat constituencies, 30 functional in 28 constituencies, 40 Election Committee). The colonial council held its first indirect elections in 1985 and 1988 (functional constituencies and an electoral college of District Board and municipal council members), its first direct elections in 1991, and its last in 1995. The election due 6 September 2020 was postponed by the Chief Executive in Council and never held. By-elections fill casual vacancies.

classes.locator: https://www.basiclaw.gov.hk/en/basiclaw/annex1.html (the Chief Executive is elected by a broadly representative Election Committee of 1,500 members; term of office five years)
classes.note: Elected by secret ballot of the Election Committee (800 members in 2002-2007, 1,200 in 2012-2017, 1,500 from 2021; the 400-member Selection Committee chose the first Chief Executive on 11 December 1996). In 2002 and 2005 the sole validly nominated candidate was declared elected and no poll was held. A vacancy is filled by an election within six months (Basic Law Article 53), as in 2005.

classes.name: 鄉郊代表選舉
classes.note: Under the Rural Representative Election Ordinance (Cap. 576) every existing village returns one Resident Representative, every indigenous or composite indigenous village one to five Indigenous Inhabitant Representatives, and the market towns of Cheung Chau and Peng Chau 39 and 17 Kaifong Representatives by block vote. 1,540 seats in 2023, of which 1,100 were returned uncontested and 115 failed for want of a candidate. The Home Affairs Department runs the elections on several January Sundays every four years; the EAC reports each one and publishes results by village. Before 2003 villages chose representatives under rural committee rules, not public law (left out). Rural by-elections are held about twice a year.

classes.name: 區議會（區議局）選舉
classes.note: The colonial District Boards (18 or 19 boards) were first elected in 1982 (New Territories in March, urban areas in September), then in 1985, 1988, 1991, and 1994, by first past the post in single- and two-member constituencies alongside appointed members until 1994. Appointed Provisional District Boards served from 1997 and the District Councils replaced them on 1 January 2000.
classes.disposition_reason: No official online canvass found: the results were published as Government Gazette notices and in the Boundary and Election Commission's reports, neither of which the Hong Kong government serves online for 1982-1994; the class waits on a scan of the Gazette or the commission's reports.

dates.note: Ordinary elections in 1982, 1985, 1988, 1991, and 1994.

classes.name: 市政局選舉
classes.note: The Urban Council (1936-1999) had elected members from 1952 on a restricted franchise, widened to universal suffrage in 1983; its last election was in 1995. A provisional council appointed in 1997 served until both municipal councils were dissolved on 31 December 1999 by the Provision of Municipal Services (Reorganization) Ordinance (Cap. 552). Its predecessor, the Sanitary Board, had elected members from 1888 to 1935 (class sanitary_board).
classes.disposition_reason: No official online canvass found: results 1952-1995 were published as Government Gazette notices and in Urban Council and Boundary and Election Commission reports, none of which an official Hong Kong host serves online; the class waits on a scan.

dates.note: Elections roughly every two years from 1952 to 1983, then 1986, 1989, 1991, and 1995.

classes.name: 區域市政局選舉
classes.note: The Regional Council served the New Territories from 1986, with directly elected members chosen in 1986, 1989, 1991, and 1995, and was dissolved with the Urban Council on 31 December 1999.
classes.disposition_reason: No official online canvass found for 1986-1995; the results were Government Gazette notices and Boundary and Election Commission reports that no official Hong Kong host serves online.

dates.note: Elections in 1986, 1989, 1991, and 1995.

classes.name: 潔淨局選舉
classes.note: The Sanitary Board, the Urban Council's predecessor, had two (later four) members elected from 1888 by ratepayers on the jury list, the colony's first public elections; it became the Urban Council in 1936.
classes.disposition_reason: The only official record is the Hong Kong Government Gazette of 1888-1935, which no official Hong Kong host serves online; the electorate was a few hundred jurors.

dates.note: Elections to the Sanitary Board's elected seats.

classes.name: 臨時立法會選舉
classes.note: The 400-member Selection Committee chose the 60 members of the Provisional Legislative Council on 21 December 1996; the council sat from 1997 until the first Legislative Council took office on 1 July 1998.
classes.disposition_reason: Held in Shenzhen by the Selection Committee convened by the National People's Congress's Preparatory Committee, outside Hong Kong electoral law; no Hong Kong electoral authority conducted it or published its count.

classes.name: 香港特別行政區選舉全國人民代表大會代表
classes.name_en: HKSAR deputies to the National People's Congress
classes.note: 36 deputies elected every five years by an electoral conference of Hong Kong members (from 2017 the Election Committee members and others).
classes.disposition_reason: Conducted by a presidium under the National People's Congress Standing Committee's rules, not by the Hong Kong electoral authorities; an indirect vote of a conference of a few thousand members. It belongs to China's census if anywhere.

classes.name: 鄉事委員會及鄉議局選舉
classes.name_en: Rural committee and Heung Yee Kuk elections
classes.note: Village and kaifong representatives elect each of the 27 rural committees' chairmen and executive committees, and the committee chairmen and others form the Heung Yee Kuk's council.
classes.disposition_reason: Internal elections of statutory advisory bodies held under their own constitutions and the Heung Yee Kuk Ordinance (Cap. 1097), not by the Electoral Affairs Commission or the Home Affairs Department, and with no published count.

classes.name: 公投
classes.disposition_reason: Neither the Basic Law nor any Hong Kong ordinance provides for a referendum, and none has been held. The 2014 civil referendum was a private poll, and the 2010 Legislative Council by-elections that the resigning members called a referendum were ordinary by-elections (class legco).

classes.name: 初選
classes.disposition_reason: No law provides for a state-run nominating contest; candidates are nominated by subscribers (and from 2021 by Election Committee members), and the 2020 opposition primary was a private poll.
